blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Chhattisgarh accounts for a major proportion of India's tribal population, comprising 42 officially recognized Scheduled Tribes with multiple sub-castes.
The Gond tribe constitutes the largest tribal demographic in Chhattisgarh, followed by Kanwar, Oraon, and Halba tribes.
The state hosts 7 Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs): 5 central (Abujhmaria, Baiga, Birhor, Kamar, Hill Korwa) and 2 state-recognized (Pando, Bhunjia).
The Ghotul system functions as a socio-cultural learning center and youth dormitory predominantly among the Muria tribe of Bastar.
Historical tribal resistance in Chhattisgarh includes major movements such as the Halba Rebellion (1774–79), Paralkot Revolt (1825), and the historic Bhumkal Revolt of 1910.

blocks.content: Chhattisgarh is one of the most tribal-dominated states in India. According to the Census 2011, Scheduled Tribes constitute approximately 30.6% of the state's total population. The state has 42 recognized Scheduled Tribes. Of these, 5 tribes are designated as Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs), formerly known as Primitive Tribal Groups (PTGs).
The Ghotul system represents a traditional youth dormitory institution central to the socio-cultural fabric of the Muria tribe in Bastar.

blocks.content: The Ghotul is a unique dormitory system practised by the Muria tribe of Bastar. It is a youth institution where boys (Chelik) and girls (Motiari) live together in a separate building (Ghotul) and learn tribal customs, culture, dances, and music. The Ghotul serves as a social institution for the education and socialization of tribal youth. Each Ghotul is governed by elected leaders - the head boy is called 'Silledar' and the head girl is called 'Belosa'.

Several tribal communities in Chhattisgarh have revolted against oppression throughout history. The Bhumkal revolt (1910) led by Gundadhur against British rule is the most celebrated. The Muriya revolt, the Halba revolt, and various other uprisings reflect the spirit of resistance among the tribal communities. Tribals of Chhattisgarh observe 'Bhumkal Diwas' on 10 February every year to commemorate the 1910 revolt.
